newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Jun/Jul gas oil trades at -3cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Jun/Jul gas oil trades at -3cts.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil inter-front months swaps slipped into contango at midday on Thursday following an onslaught of prompt physical offers at considerably lower prices on Wednesday, traders said.
"Gas oil is under pressure because there are a lot of unsold prompt barrels around," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $24.60/$24.70 per barrel while July was at $24.65/$24.75, down slightly from Wednesday's quotes, brokers said.
The June/July spread traded earlier in the day minus 3 cents, they said.
Traders said the weaker front month was due to a prompt overhang in Singapore and distressed cargoes in China.

In the Singapore physical market, sellers emerged late Wednesday to offer their barrels aggressively with a 150,000-barrel cargo traded at $24.50 per barrel for June 19-23 lifting, down 40 cents from Tuesday's offered level for a cargo loading at similar dates.
Offers for end June/early July barrels were also lower at $24.80 per barrel from Tuesday's traded level of $25.30 per barrel.
Traders said sellers came out strongly after news of poor demand from China where up to four prompt cargoes of around 30,000 tonnes each are still unsold.
The market is also concerned following reports that up to four 60,000 to 80,0000 tonne tankers are headed to this region for arrival in early July.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted in a wide range at $100.00/$101.50 as buyers dropped their bids in the face of further cuts to crude levels.
Overnight July Brent crude closed down 18 cents to $18.72 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange in the wake of bearish API data.
